1.label: very_easy
1.summary: Match one card to one reader, then find a broad single swipe tempo without static interference.
1.natural_language: Match the single card to its badge reader. Use the test feedback to find its broad swipe tempo, then run the audit.

2.label: easy
2.summary: Assign two cards and calibrate two broad, distinct swipe tempos with denser, straighter swipes than L1.
2.natural_language: Match both cards to their badge readers. Calibrate each reader from the arrow end with a dense, straight, monotonic swipe, then run the audit.

3.label: medium
3.summary: Handle three badge assignments and three separated tempos under moderate dense-swipe path tolerances.
3.natural_language: Match all three cards. Calibrate the three readers by using their feedback and keeping every arrow-to-arrow swipe dense, straight, and monotonic.

4.label: hard
4.summary: Preserve the current three-reader desk: three badge assignments, three hidden tempos, the legacy off-rail static display layout, and the existing dense straight swipe requirements.
4.natural_language: Insert each card into the reader with the matching badge. Then swipe from the illuminated arrow end to the other end in one straight, monotonic motion. Each reader wants a different hidden speed; use TOO FAST, TOO SLOW, and BAD READ feedback until all three lock, then run the audit.

5.label: very_hard
5.summary: Match and calibrate four compact readers with four narrow tempos, three lane-blocking static fields each, and tighter dense-swipe geometry.
5.natural_language: Match four cards to four badge readers. Learn all four narrow tempos while threading every dense swipe past three static fields, then run the audit.

simplified.summary: Select a card, use the matching reader's Insert selected card control, set a visible test duration, and execute the visible clearance-route swipe proxy. The generated reader, feedback, timing window, and replayed path checks remain the same.

full.summary: Drag each card into its matching physical slot, then hold and move the reader handle from its illuminated arrow end to the opposite end with a timed, dense, straight pointer path.
